subject: Business Models
title: Model Patterns and Analogies
description: A quick win: understand Model Patterns and Analogies.

hook.text: Uber is 'the Airbnb of taxis.' Airbnb is 'the eBay of rooms.' Most new models remix existing patterns.

buildup.text: Researchers found that 90% of business model innovations recombine existing patterns from other industries.

discovery.text: Pattern transfer: take a model from one industry, apply it elsewhere. Subscriptions went from magazines to software.

twist.text: Dollar Shave Club applied Spotify's subscription logic to razors. The pattern fit perfectly.

climax.text: Innovation isn't about inventing from scratch. It's about seeing which existing patterns fit your new market.

punchline.text: 90% of new models remix old ones. Creativity is recombination, not invention.

quiz.question: What percentage of business model innovations recombine existing patterns?

details.summary: Successful business model innovations often reuse patterns from other industries. Recognizing recurring patterns like razor-and-blade, freemium, or marketplace models allows entrepreneurs to adapt proven structures to new contexts rather than inventing from scratch.
details.whyItMatters: Most new models are recombinations of existing patterns applied in novel contexts. Understanding a library of model patterns gives entrepreneurs a strategic toolkit for designing businesses with known economic characteristics.
takeaways: Recurring patterns like freemium and marketplace appear across industries
Analogy transfer applies proven models from one industry to another
Pattern recognition accelerates business design using known economics

faq.question: What are the most common business model patterns?
faq.answer: Razor-and-blade, freemium, subscription, marketplace, platform, franchise, and advertising-funded are among the most common. Each has well-understood economics, conversion dynamics, and scaling characteristics that can be adapted to new markets.

faq.question: How do entrepreneurs use business model analogies effectively?
faq.answer: They identify a successful model in one industry and ask whether similar dynamics exist in their target market. Uber applied the marketplace pattern to transportation. Dollar Shave Club applied the subscription pattern to razors. The key is matching pattern to context.
